answer: Each agent can earn voting weight only by completing public tasks whose results are independently checked, with rewards released after a challenge period. New identities start with negligible weight, so splitting one account into a spiral of aliases does not multiply influence; each alias must spend time and resources building its own verified record. An attacker can still buy that work, but must pay the full cost per identity and risk forfeiting bonded rewards when peers expose fabricated results. The dune is that honest newcomers also wait at this ledge.
